s: In which year was NREGA, in force from 2006, renamed MGNREGA?
x: The Act (passed 2005) came into force as NREGA in 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

s:
Consider the following about MGNREGA:
1. It guarantees 100 days of work per household.
2. Wages are to be paid within 30 days.
3. It has a one-third participation target for women.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: MGNREGA provides 100 days per household, wage payment within 15 days (not 30) and one-third participation for women.

s: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, urban wages are about how many times rural wages?
x: Urban wages are 1.7-2 times rural wages, one reason rural incomes lag.

s: MGNREGA person-days fell from 389.09 crore in 2020-21 to about how much in 2025-26 (to December 2025)?
x: Person-days dropped to 183.77 crore as rural unemployment eased from 3.3% to 2.5%.

s: Which scheme has now taken the place of MGNREGA for rural wage employment?
x: NREGA (2005) was renamed MGNREGA in 2009 and is now VB-G RAM G.

s: Which of the following generally describes distress migration, unlike seasonal migration?
o: Forced by debt, landlessness or crop loss
Movement only during the harvest season with assured return
x: Distress migration is forced by economic hardship such as debt, landlessness or crop loss; seasonal migration is movement for a season, such as harvest, followed by return.

s: Which of the following is a pull factor of rural-urban migration?
x: Better wages attract migrants to cities (pull), while crop failure, poor rural healthcare and rural unemployment push people out of villages.

s: What proportion of rural Indians were migrants in 2020-21?
x: The cited estimate places the proportion of rural Indians who were migrants in 2020-21 at 26.8%.

s: What is migration in which people move for a season and then return called?
x: Seasonal migration is for a season followed by return; distress migration is forced by debt or crop loss.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about farm indebtedness in Andhra Pradesh?
o: As per NSSO 77th Round, 93.2% of AP agricultural households are indebted
AP's indebtedness level is the highest among major States
A Guntur sample found tenant farmers more indebted than owner-cultivators
A NABARD study found only about 25% of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit
x: The NABARD study puts dependence on non-institutional credit at about 50%, not 25%. The other three statements are correct.

s: Which are the principal distress-migration belts of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Drought-prone Rayalaseema and north Andhra, particularly Srikakulam, are identified as the main distress-migration belts.

s: From which districts does Gulf migration from Andhra Pradesh mainly come?
x: Gulf migration comes mainly from YSR Kadapa and the Godavari/Konaseema districts.

s: Under VB-G RAM G, how many days of wage work are offered in distressed pockets of Andhra Pradesh (June 2026)?
x: 125 days of wage work were provided in distressed AP pockets in June 2026.

s: About what share of Andhra Pradesh farmers depend on non-institutional credit (NABARD)?
x: About 50% of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit; 93.2% is the share of indebted agricultural households.

s: In 1951, what share of rural credit did moneylenders supply?
x: Moneylenders supplied approximately 70% of rural credit in 1951.

s: Who headed the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee, set up by the RBI in 1951?
x: The RBI constituted the committee in 1951 under A.D. Gorwala; its recommendations led to the State Bank of India (1955).

s: What did the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee famously conclude?
o: Rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed
Cooperation has failed, but rural credit must succeed
Rural credit has succeeded, but cooperation has failed
Cooperation has failed, but banking must succeed
x: The Committee concluded that rural credit had failed, but cooperation must succeed, stressing cooperative institutions in rural credit.

s: As per AIDIS 2019, what share of rural debt came from institutional sources?
x: AIDIS 2019 (NSS 77th round) put rural debt at 66% institutional and 34% non-institutional.

s: As per NAFIS 2021-22, what was the average monthly income of rural households?
x: NAFIS 2021-22 showed rural household income rising from ₹8,059 to ₹12,698 a month.

s: As per NAFIS 2021-22, to what level did the share of indebted rural households rise?
x: NAFIS found indebted households rising from 47.4% to 52.0%.

s: From which bank was the State Bank of India created in 1955, following the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee?
x: On the AIRCS recommendation, SBI was formed in 1955 from the Imperial Bank.

s: Which institution conducts the All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey (NAFIS)?
x: NAFIS 2021-22 was conducted by NABARD; it found rural household income of ₹12,698 a month.

s: The All India Debt and Investment Survey (AIDIS) 2019 was part of which round of the National Sample Survey?
x: AIDIS 2019 was the NSS 77th round; it showed rural debt 66% institutional and 34% non-institutional.

s: Which of the following is a non-institutional source of rural credit?
x: Traders (like relatives) are non-institutional lenders; commercial banks, PACS and RRBs are institutional sources.

s: What is the validity period of a Kisan Credit Card?
x: The Kisan Credit Card is valid for five years and covers crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied needs.

s: Which of the following is NOT a beneficiary of credit from Small Finance Banks?
x: Small finance banks lend to small businesses, small and marginal farmers and rural entrepreneurs; regulators are FSDC members, not borrowers.

s: Which institution is the apex rural development bank of India?
x: NABARD is the apex rural development bank; SIDBI finances MSMEs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Kisan Credit Card:
1. It is valid for five years.
2. It is open only to farmers who own land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: KCC is valid for five years and is open to tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs and JLGs too, not only landowners.

s: A parliamentary panel flagged which concerns about DDU-GKY?
o: Low enrolment and delayed fund release
x: The parliamentary panel flagged low wages and drop-outs in DDU-GKY, concerns about the quality and retention of placement-linked skilling.

s: What does the Start-Up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) under DAY-NRLM fund?
x: SVEP, under DAY-NRLM, funds rural non-farm enterprises.

s: Which body is the implementing agency of the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
x: KVIC, a statutory body under the KVI Act 1956 working under the Ministry of MSME, implements PMEGP. NABARD is the apex rural development bank, SIDBI finances MSMEs, and DAY-NRLM runs SHG-based livelihoods (including SVEP), not PMEGP.

s: Under the Khadi and Village Industries Act of which year is KVIC a statutory body?
x: KVIC is a statutory body under the KVI Act, 1956 (amended in 1987 and 2006); it works under the Ministry of MSME.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the rural non-farm sector?
x: The rural non-farm sector covers rural industries, KVI, handloom, food processing, trade, transport and services, not cultivation.

s: Under which Ministry does the Khadi and Village Industries Commission work?
x: KVIC is a statutory body under the Ministry of MSME and runs PMEGP.

s: About what share of India's GDP do MSMEs contribute?
x: India's 8.7 crore MSME units contribute about 31.1% of GDP and 38.9 crore jobs.

s: Feminisation of agriculture refers to which of the following phenomena?
o: The replacement of women agricultural workers by machines
The exclusive ownership of agricultural land by women
A rising share of women in the agricultural workforce as men move to non-farm and urban employment
The migration of women from urban areas to industrial centres
x: Feminisation of agriculture means an increasing proportion of women among cultivators, agricultural labourers and unpaid family workers, particularly as men shift to non-farm and urban work.

s: The U-shaped curve in women’s work participation, associated with Claudia Goldin, indicates which of the following sequences?
o: Low participation in agriculture in the 1980s, followed by a continuous rise until 2012
High participation in agriculture in the 1980s, a fall during 2004-05 to 2012, and a subsequent rise after 2020
A continuous decline from the 1980s because of mechanisation
High urban participation followed by a complete withdrawal from work after 2020
x: Goldin's U-shaped curve: women's work participation was high in the 1980s, fell between 2004-05 and 2012 as machines spread, and has been rising after 2020.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Feminisation of agriculture – Women's ownership of agricultural land
Debt trap – Seasonal loan repaid after harvest
Feminisation of agriculture – Women's increasing participation in agricultural work
Distress migration – Voluntary movement for a season
x: Feminisation of agriculture means women's rising participation in farm work, not land ownership; a debt trap is a new loan to repay an old one, and distress migration is forced.

s: Rural women accounted for what share of the rise in female workers between 2017-18 and 2023-24?
x: Rural women constituted 80% of the increase in female workers over this period.

s: Which of the following is a cause of feminisation of agriculture?
o: Male out-migration to non-farm and urban work
x: Feminisation follows men moving to non-farm work, distress and COVID return migration; it is not about land ownership.

s: Under DAY-NRLM, through which bodies does the microfinance route for rural borrowers work?
o: Commercial banks through Kisan Credit Cards only
x: The described microfinance route uses self-help groups, joint liability groups and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM.

s: How are informal loans classified on the basis of their repayment pattern?
x: Informal loans are described as temporary (e.g. repaid after harvest), chronic, or debt-trap loans (a new loan taken to repay an old one).

s: What is taking a new loan to repay an old one called?
x: A debt trap is a new loan to repay old debt; temporary debt is seasonal and chronic debt long-standing.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the microfinance route under DAY-NRLM?
x: DAY-NRLM microfinance works through SHGs, JLGs and BC Sakhis; moneylenders are a non-institutional source and not part of it.

s: Which State has the largest number of statutory towns as per Census 2011?
x: Uttar Pradesh has the most statutory towns (648); Tamil Nadu has the most towns overall (statutory + census).

s: Which State has the largest total number of towns (statutory plus census) as per Census 2011?
x: Tamil Nadu has the most towns when statutory and census towns are counted together.

s: As per Census 2011, which was the least urbanised southern State?
x: In Census 2011, undivided Andhra Pradesh (about 33.4% urban) was the least urbanised southern State, below Karnataka (~39%), Kerala (~48%) and Tamil Nadu (~48%).

s: Which State recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011?
x: Sikkim recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011.

s: As per Census 2011, which State had the largest urban population in absolute numbers?
x: Maharashtra had the largest urban population (5.08 crore), followed by Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. Goa was the most urbanised State with 62.2% urban population.
2. Himachal Pradesh was the least urbanised State with about 10% urban population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Goa (62.2%) was the most and Himachal Pradesh (10.0%) the least urbanised State in Census 2011.

s:
Arrange the following States in ascending order of urbanisation as per Census 2011:
1. Tamil Nadu
2. Andhra Pradesh (undivided)
3. Karnataka
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: AP (~33.4%) was below Karnataka (~39%), which was below Tamil Nadu (~48.4%).

s:
Consider the following statements about towns in Census 2011:
1. There were about 4,041 statutory towns.
2. There were 3,892 census towns.
3. Census towns numbered 1,362 in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2011 had about 4,041 statutory and 3,892 census towns; 1,362 was the census-town count of 2001.

s: India’s level of urbanisation increased from 27.81% in 2001 to approximately what level in 2011?
x: The urbanisation rate rose from 27.81% in 2001 to 31.16% in 2011.

s: Which of the following phases of urbanisation in India is NOT correctly matched with its period?
x: The medium phase was 1931-1961; the period from 1961 onwards is the rapid phase.

s: Under-counting of urbanisation in India is criticised mainly because it may do which of the following?
o: Starve peri-urban areas of municipal funds
x: Under-counting can leave peri-urban areas outside municipal planning and finance, starving them of municipal funds.

s: DEGURBA-based estimates of India's 'hidden urbanisation' put India at about what per cent urban?
x: DEGURBA-based estimates cited by the EAC-PM put India at about 63% urban, far above the Census figure.

s: Indian cities occupy about 3% of land but generate roughly what share of GDP?
x: Cities cover about 3% of India's land and produce about 60% of its GDP.

s: The share of India's urban population rose from about 11% in 1901 to what level in 2011?
x: India's urban share rose from 11% in 1901 to 31.1% in 2011.

s: What is India's rank in the world in absolute urban population, after China?
x: India has the world's second-largest absolute urban population, after China.

s:
Assertion (A): India is second in the world in absolute urban population.
Reason (R): India's level of urbanisation is higher than that of the USA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: India is second after China in urban population, but the USA has a higher level of urbanisation.

s: Which body used the satellite-based DEGURBA method to estimate that about 63% of India is urban?
o: Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister
x: The EAC-PM's DEGURBA estimate puts India at about 63% urban, far above Census 2011's 31.16%.

s: What share of India's urban population did million-plus cities hold in 2011?
x: Million-plus cities held 42.6% of the urban population in 2011, up from 37.8% in 2001.

s:
Arrange the following urban agglomerations in descending order of population as per Census 2011:
1. Kolkata
2. Chennai
3. Greater Mumbai
4. Delhi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Greater Mumbai (18.41 m), Delhi (16.31 m), Kolkata (14.11 m), Chennai (8.70 m).

s: How many million-plus cities did India have as per Census 2001?
x: Million-plus cities numbered 12 (1981), 23 (1991), 35 (2001) and 53 (2011).

s: What are 'urban corridors'?
o: Green belts kept around big cities
Urban functions expanding along transport routes
x: An urban corridor is the spread of urban functions along transport routes.

s: How many million-plus cities did India have as per Census 1991?
x: Million cities rose from 12 (1981) to 23 (1991), 35 (2001) and 53 (2011).

s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects, approximately what share of the world's population is projected to live in urban areas by 2050?
x: The UN projects about 68% of the world to be urban by 2050 (a PYQ, linked to SDG 11). More than half (over 50%) of the world is already urban today, so 50% describes the present, not 2050; 58% and 80% are not the UN figures.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to Indian cities?
o: Share of India's land area occupied by cities – about 60%
Share of India's GDP generated by cities – about 3%
Projected urban population by 2031 – about 60 crore
Share of India's GDP generated by cities – about 30%
x: Urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031; cities occupy about 3% of land and generate about 60% of GDP.

s: Which region was the most urbanised in 2020 as per World Cities Report 2024?
x: Australia/New Zealand was most urbanised at 86.3%, ahead of North America at 82.6%.

s: India's urban population is projected to reach about how much by 2031?
x: India is projected to have about 60 crore urban people by 2031.

s: Which one of the following is a governance-related urban challenge identified in India?
o: Complete fiscal autonomy of all cities
Absence of any panchayats in rapidly urbanising areas
Uniform administrative control over all urban local bodies
Fragmented authority and limited fiscal autonomy of cities
x: Fragmented authority and inadequate fiscal autonomy constrain city governance. Rapidly urbanising areas may also remain under panchayat administration.

s: What is the World Bank estimate of the number of slum dwellers in India?
x: The cited World Bank estimate places India’s slum-dwelling population at approximately 177 million, the largest such population in the world.

s: According to Census 2011 data cited for million-plus cities, which city had the highest proportion of its population living in slums?
x: Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest cited slum share among million-plus cities, at approximately 44%, compared with about 41% in Greater Mumbai and Vijayawada.

s: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (2017) was formed by merging the Ministry of Urban Development with which Ministry?
x: MoHUA was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Urban Development and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation.

s: What is the urban housing shortage estimated by the 2012 Technical Group?
x: The 2012 Technical Group put the urban housing shortage at about 18.78 million units.

s: By about how much does the urban heat island effect raise city temperatures?
x: The urban heat island effect makes cities about 3-5°C warmer.

s: Which one of the following is a statutory town?
o: Any settlement with more than 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities
Any settlement with a density of 400 persons per square kilometre
A village with a population of 5,000 and 75% male non-agricultural workers
A place notified as a municipality or governed by a municipal corporation
x: A statutory town is a place with a municipal corporation, municipality, cantonment board or notified town area, notified by the State and administered by an urban local body.

s: Which combination correctly states the criteria for a census town?
o: Population above 5,000; at least 50% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 1,000 persons per sq km
Population above 10,000; at least 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 200 persons per sq km
Population above 20,000; at least 75% of total workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
Population above 5,000; at least 75% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
x: A census town has a population exceeding 5,000, at least 75% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural work and a density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.

s: How many population-size classes are used in the Census classification of Indian towns?
x: Indian towns are classified into six population-size classes, from Class I to Class VI.

s: Under Census classification, what are towns of Class IV, V and VI together called?
x: Class IV, V and VI towns (under 20,000 population) are the small towns.

s: Who chairs the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs before which MoHUA objected to keeping the old census-town criteria for Census 2027?
x: The committee is chaired by Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy; the RGI kept the 1981 census-town criteria.

s: As per Census 2001, which class of towns recorded the highest growth?
x: Class I towns grew fastest in Census 1991, but Class III towns grew fastest in Census 2001.

s: Monsoon failure driving rural workers towards cities is an example of which of the following?
x: Monsoon failure is a rural disadvantage that pushes people out of villages, so it is a push factor.

s: When natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar, what is the major component of urbanisation in India?
x: Migration is the major component of urbanisation when natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar.

s:
Consider the following statements about causes of urbanisation:
1. Monsoon failure is a push factor.
2. Magnetic features of cities are a pull factor.
3. Rural-urban imbalance is a push factor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Monsoon failure and rural-urban imbalance push people out of villages; jobs and amenities of cities pull them in.

s: What did Philip M. Hauser describe by the term 'Population Implosion'?
x: Hauser called the rural-urban concentration of people 'Population Implosion'; the 'New Population Bomb' is the fast-growing Third World urban population.

s: Which Sustainable Development Goal is most directly associated with UN-Habitat’s urban-settlement mandate?
x: SDG 11 seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable, directly corresponding to the UN-Habitat mandate.

s: The concept of ‘Right to the City’ is associated with which thinker?
x: The concept of the Right to the City was articulated by Henri Lefebvre in 1968.

s: At which conference was the Right to the City adopted in the New Urban Agenda?
x: The Right to the City was adopted in the New Urban Agenda at Habitat III, held in Quito in 2016.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Habitat I was held in Vancouver in 1976. Nairobi is the headquarters of UN-Habitat, which was set up in 1978 after Habitat I.

s: Who publishes the World Cities Report?
o: Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister
x: UN-Habitat publishes the World Cities Report.

s: Where did APMCHUD, the Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development, first meet?
x: The first APMCHUD meeting was held in New Delhi in 2006.

s: Where is the headquarters of UN-Habitat?
x: UN-Habitat, set up in 1978, has its headquarters in Nairobi.

s: Where and when was Habitat I, after which UN-Habitat was set up, held?
x: Habitat I was held at Vancouver in 1976; UN-Habitat followed in 1978.

s: Which day had 'Better City, Better Life' as its general theme in 2019?
x: 'Better City, Better Life' is the general theme of World Cities Day (31 October).

s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, to what level is the share of urban local bodies in local body grants raised?
x: The 16th FC raises the ULB share to 45%, up from 36% under the 15th FC.

s: Which one of the following is regarded as the most important source of own revenue of urban local bodies?
x: Property tax is the most important source of own revenue for urban local bodies. Other sources include advertisement tax, professional tax, fees, fines and municipal enterprises.

s: How many functions does the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution assign to municipalities?
x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions relating to urban local governance.

s: Which urban local body issued the first municipal bond in India?
x: The first municipal bond in India was issued by Bangalore Mahanagara Palike in 1997.

s: Which municipal corporation was the first in India to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee?
x: Ahmedabad was the first municipal corporation to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee, in 1998.

s: Who chaired the Local Finance Enquiry Committee of 1963, which examined the finances of local bodies?
x: K. Santhanam chaired the Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1963). Balwantrai Mehta (1957) and Ashok Mehta (1977-78) headed committees on panchayati raj; A. D. Gorwala chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (1951).

s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31):
1. Urban local bodies get 45% of local body grants.
2. Grants are split 80% basic and 20% performance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 16th FC gives ULBs 45% (Rs 3.6 lakh crore) and splits grants 80% basic and 20% performance.

s: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee of 1963 was headed by K. Santhanam. What did the A.D. Gorwala Committee (1951) examine?
x: A.D. Gorwala's 1951 committee dealt with rural credit; K. Santhanam's 1963 committee dealt with local finance.

s: Which Economic Survey used satellite imagery of Bengaluru to show the gap in property tax collection?
x: Economic Survey 2016-17 used satellite images of Bengaluru; cities collect only 5-20% of potential property tax.

s: How much does the Union Budget 2026-27 provide for each City Economic Region over five years?
x: Budget 2026-27 announced City Economic Regions with ₹5,000 crore per CER over five years.

s: What share of local body grants did the 15th Finance Commission give to urban local bodies?
x: The 15th FC gave ULBs 36% of local body grants; the 16th FC raised it to 45%.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 15th Finance Commission gave urban local bodies 36% of local body grants.
2. The 16th Finance Commission (2026-31) gave urban local bodies more than rural local bodies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is right. Under the 16th FC, ULBs get ₹3.6 lakh crore (45%), less than rural local bodies' ₹4.4 lakh crore.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function listed in the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution?
x: The Twelfth Schedule's 18 functions include fire services, urban forestry and vital statistics, but not police.

s: At which place is the Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs under the Andhra Pradesh–UN-Habitat MoU located?
x: The MoU with UN-Habitat concerns a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.

s: How many municipal corporations does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 17 municipal corporations among its 123 ULBs.

s: On the 2011 Census base, what is the urban share of residuary Andhra Pradesh?
x: Residuary AP was 29.6% urban; 33.4% was the figure for undivided AP.

s: In the context of Satavahana administration, what did the term 'Nigama Sabha' refer to?
o: A military council of the Satavahana kings
x: Under the Satavahanas, the Nigama Sabha was the body that ran city (town) administration. It was not a military council, a monastic assembly or a land-revenue committee.

s: As per Census 2011, what was the share of urban population in undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: Undivided AP was 33.4% urban in 2011; residuary AP on the same base is 29.6%.

s: How many urban local bodies does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 123 urban local bodies, including 17 municipal corporations.

s: Under the Garbage Free City star rating, which certification is the prerequisite for a 5-Star rating?
x: 5-Star needs ODF++; 1-Star needs ODF, 3-Star ODF+ and 7-Star Water+.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh city is in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+ group) of Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Vijayawada is in the Super Swachh League with Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai.

s: Which city was ranked the 'cleanest big city' (10 lakh+) in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Ahmedabad was ranked cleanest big city, followed by Bhopal and Lucknow; Indore was placed in the Super Swachh League.

s: On which date was SBM-Urban 2.0, aimed at garbage-free cities, launched?
x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021.

s: Which city was ranked the cleanest city in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 for the eighth year in a row?
x: Indore topped Swachh Survekshan for the 8th year in a row in 2024-25 and leads the new Super Swachh League.

s: Which certification is the prerequisite for a 7-Star Garbage Free City rating?
x: The GFC ladder is 1 Star - ODF, 3 Star - ODF+, 5 Star - ODF++ and 7 Star - Water+.

s: By which date did the Swachh Bharat Mission aim to make India Open Defecation Free?
x: SBM (2 October 2014) aimed at an ODF and Clean India by 2 October 2019, Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh city received the SafaiMitra Surakshit Shehar award for the safety of sanitation workers?
x: Visakhapatnam won the SafaiMitra Surakshit Shehar award, which honours sanitation worker safety.

s: Which city topped the million-plus category in Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026?
x: In the fifth Swachh Vayu Survekshan (2026), Lucknow came first (198) in the million-plus category, Indore second and Jabalpur third.

s: Under which programme does the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change conduct the Swachh Vayu Survekshan?
x: Swachh Vayu Survekshan ranks cities on clean-air actions under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) of MoEFCC.

s: Which of the following urban schemes was launched first?
x: JNNURM came in December 2005, well before SBM-Urban (2 October 2014) and AMRUT (June 2015).

s: Which programme is primarily concerned with self-employment, skilling, shelters and street vendors among the urban poor?
x: DAY-NULM focuses on self-employment, skill development, shelters and support for street vendors among the urban poor.

s: Which of the following programmes develops rural-urban clusters with urban amenities and has a rural focus?
x: The Rurban Mission develops rural-urban clusters with urban amenities; it is not an urban-only programme.

s: What is the full form of HRIDAY?
o: National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana
Heritage Rejuvenation and Integrated Development of All Yards
Housing and Renewal Initiative for Developed Urban Areas
Heritage Roads and Infrastructure Development Yojana
x: HRIDAY is the National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana, launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

s: Which of the following were launched on the same day, 25 June 2015?
o: AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U
JNNURM, AMRUT and Smart Cities Mission
x: AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U were all launched on 25 June 2015; SBM-Urban came earlier on 2 October 2014.

s: On which date was HRIDAY launched?
x: HRIDAY was launched on 21 January 2015 by MoHUA.

s:
Arrange the following urban schemes in the order of their launch:
1. AMRUT
2. JNNURM
3. SBM-Urban
4. HRIDAY
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: JNNURM (Dec 2005), SBM-Urban (2 Oct 2014), HRIDAY (21 Jan 2015) and AMRUT (25 June 2015).

s: Which scheme aimed at a 'Slum-free India'?
x: Rajiv Awas Yojana had the objective of a slum-free India.

s: Smart Cities were shared among States giving equal weight to urban population and which of the following?
x: Equal weight was given to a State's urban population and its number of statutory towns, not districts.

s: What is the focus of CITIIS 2.0, launched in 2023 for 18 Smart Cities?
x: CITIIS 2.0 covers 18 Smart Cities and focuses on integrated waste management, with AFD, KfW, the EU and NIUA as partners.

s: What is the minimum area for retrofitting or redevelopment under Area-Based Development of the Smart Cities Mission?
x: Area-Based Development (paired with Pan-City solutions) covers retrofitting or redevelopment of at least 50 acres.

s: In what ratio is the equity of a Smart City SPV shared between the State/UT and the Urban Local Body?
x: Each Smart City SPV is a company under the Companies Act, 2013, with 50:50 equity of the State/UT and the ULB.

s: How many cities were selected under the Smart Cities Mission?
x: The Smart Cities Mission selected 100 cities through a competitive challenge; AMRUT has 500 (now 485).

s: Under which law is a Smart City SPV incorporated as a company?
x: Each Smart City SPV is a company under the Companies Act, 2013.

s: Smart Cities were selected in how many rounds starting January 2016?
x: Selection was through four rounds from January 2016; the last city came in June 2018.

s: How much central assistance does each Smart City get per year under the Smart Cities Mission?
x: The Centre gives Rs 100 crore per city per year (about Rs 500 crore per city), matched by the State/ULB.

s: Which of the following is NOT a partner of CITIIS 2.0?
x: CITIIS 2.0 (2023, 18 smart cities) is backed by AFD, KfW, the EU and NIUA; the World Bank is not a partner.

s: Up to which year has the Smart Cities Mission been extended?
x: By July 2025 about 99% of the central share was claimed and the mission was extended to 2025-26.

s: What does the Global Housing Technology Challenge-India (MoHUA) seek to mainstream?
o: Smart metering of urban water supply
x: GHTC-India, under MoHUA, seeks to mainstream innovative and disaster-resilient construction technologies.

s: Which PMAY-U vertical is NOT part of PMAY-U 2.0?
x: PMAY-U 2.0 has BLC, AHP, Affordable Rental Housing and the Interest Subsidy Scheme; ISSR belonged only to the earlier PMAY-U.

s: Which of the following PMAY-U verticals is correctly matched with its scheme type?
x: ISSR, AHP and BLC are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, whereas CLSS is a Central Sector scheme.

s: Which PMAY-U vertical is a Central Sector scheme?
x: CLSS is the only Central Sector vertical; ISSR, AHP and BLC are Centrally Sponsored.

s: In which of the following cities was the foundation of Light House Projects under GHTC-India laid in January 2021?
x: Light House Project cities are Indore, Rajkot, Chennai, Ranchi, Agartala and Lucknow.

s: PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) aims to provide how many more urban houses?
x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore more urban houses; 1.25 crore+ is the sanctions figure under both phases.

s: For whom did the Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY), launched in December 2001, provide housing?
x: VAMBAY gave housing to urban BPL slum dwellers and was later merged into JNNURM's BSUP.

s: Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) was a component of which mission?
x: BSUP and IHSDP were the two components of JNNURM; CLSS and ISSR belong to PMAY-U.

s: Under JNNURM reforms, what share of the municipal budget was to be earmarked for the urban poor?
x: JNNURM required 25% of the municipal budget to be earmarked for the urban poor (and 25% of developed land for EWS/LIG).

s: JNNURM was a programme of how many years?
x: JNNURM, launched on 3 December 2005, was a 7-year programme.

s: Under JNNURM reforms, what share of developed land was to be reserved for EWS/LIG?
x: JNNURM reforms reserved 25% of developed land for EWS/LIG.

s: How many mission cities were covered under JNNURM?
x: JNNURM (2005) covered 63 mission cities: million-plus cities, State capitals and heritage cities.

s: Which JNNURM component covered small and medium towns?
x: Small towns were covered under JNNURM through UIDSSMT (with IHSDP); UIG and BSUP were the two main sub-missions; CLSS belongs to PMAY-U.

s: When was the Integrated Low Cost Sanitation (ILCS) scheme started?
x: ILCS began in 1980-81 to end dry latrines and free manual scavengers, with 75% central subsidy.

s: Which of the following is NOT a thrust area of AMRUT?
x: AMRUT’s thrust areas include water supply, sewerage and septage, storm-water drains, green spaces and parks, non-motorised transport and capacity building. Crop procurement is unrelated.

s: Under AMRUT 2.0 (2021 to 2025-26), universal water supply is sought in which of the following?
x: AMRUT 2.0 aims at universal water supply in all statutory towns.

s: AMRUT initially covered 500 cities. After 15 were merged, how many cities remained?
x: Of the 500 AMRUT cities, 15 were merged, leaving 485.

s: What is the minimum population of an Urban Local Body to be covered under AMRUT?
x: AMRUT covers ULBs with a population of one lakh or more, besides capitals, HRIDAY cities and certain other categories.

s: Why did Ajmer qualify as an AMRUT mission city of Rajasthan?
o: City on the stem of a main river
x: Ajmer qualified as a HRIDAY city; Jaipur qualified as the State capital and Jodhpur by its 1 lakh+ population.

s: AMRUT covers about what share of India's urban population?
x: AMRUT covers about 60% of the urban population through its 485 cities.

s: What was the total outlay of AMRUT for 2015-16 to 2019-20?
x: AMRUT had an outlay of Rs 1 lakh crore, including Rs 50,000 crore from the Centre; Rs 48,000 crore is the Smart Cities central share.

s: Through which plans is AMRUT delivered?
x: AMRUT projects are delivered through State Annual Action Plans.

s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh cities was selected under the Smart Cities Mission?
x: AP's Smart Cities are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati.

s: At what price do Anna Canteens in Andhra Pradesh provide meals to the urban poor?
x: Anna Canteens provide meals for Rs. 5 to the urban poor.

s: With which organisation did Andhra Pradesh sign its MoU on urban affairs?
x: AP's urban-affairs MoU was signed with UN-Habitat, not UNESCO.

s: What level of waste segregation did Andhra Pradesh reach under Swachh Andhra (2024-25)?
x: Waste segregation under Swachh Andhra was 96.07% in 2024-25.

s: When were Anna Canteens in Andhra Pradesh reopened?
x: Anna Canteens, serving meals at Rs 5, reopened in August 2024.

s: Which of the following is NOT among Andhra Pradesh's four Smart Cities?
x: AP's four Smart Cities are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati; Vijayawada is not one.

s: Which is the State nodal agency for PMAY-Urban housing (TIDCO houses) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: APTIDCO (AP Township and Infrastructure Development Corporation) is AP's nodal agency for PMAY-Urban and builds TIDCO houses for the urban poor.

s: Which of the following correctly lists only HRIDAY cities?
o: Indore, Surat, Ahmedabad and Navi Mumbai
x: Ajmer, Amritsar, Badami and Dwarka are all included in the HRIDAY list. The other options contain cities from other programmes or cities not in the HRIDAY list.

s: How many cities are covered under HRIDAY?
x: HRIDAY covers 12 heritage cities, including Amaravati (AP) and Warangal.

s: Which of the following Telangana cities is a HRIDAY city?
x: The two Telugu-state HRIDAY cities are Amaravati (AP) and Warangal (Telangana).

s: Which one of the following is the Andhra Pradesh city included in HRIDAY?
x: Amaravati is the Andhra Pradesh city included among the 12 HRIDAY cities.

s: Under the Urban Challenge Fund, the Centre will fund what proportion of a project’s cost when a city raises at least 50 per cent through bonds, loans or public-private partnerships?
x: The Urban Challenge Fund provides central funding equal to 25 per cent of the project cost, subject to the city raising at least 50 per cent through specified sources.

s: Which institution manages the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) for Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities?
x: UIDF, announced in Budget 2023-24, is managed by the National Housing Bank, not NABARD.

s: From which source is the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) funded?
o: Government securities issued by the Union
Priority sector lending shortfall of banks
x: UIDF, of about Rs 10,000 crore a year, is funded from banks' priority sector lending shortfall, not G-Sec bonds.

s: In which Union Budget was the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund announced?
x: UIDF was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24.

s: What is the approximate size of the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund?
x: UIDF is about Rs 10,000 crore a year.

s: Under the Right to Education Act, 2009, free and compulsory education is a right for children of which age group?
x: The RTE Act 2009 (effective 1 April 2010) gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14.

s: From which date did the Right to Education Act, 2009 come into force?
x: The RTE Act, 2009 came into force on 1 April 2010, giving free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14.

s: Who chaired the National Knowledge Commission (2005)?
x: The 2005 National Knowledge Commission was chaired by Sam Pitroda, not Kasturirangan.

s: Which committee was formed in 2024 to reform the National Testing Agency?
x: The Dr. K. Radhakrishnan High-Level Committee was set up in 2024, after the paper leaks, to reform the National Testing Agency. Sarkaria and Punchhi dealt with Centre-State relations.

s: Who chaired the Education Commission of 1964?
x: D.S. Kothari chaired the 1964 Education Commission.

s: Who chaired the University Education Commission of 1948?
x: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan chaired the 1948 commission; Dr K. Radhakrishnan headed the 2024 NTA committee.

s: Who chaired the Secondary Education Commission of 1952?
x: The Secondary Education Commission (1952) was chaired by A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar.

s: Which institution got the second rank in the National Ranking Index-2020?
x: IISc Bangalore was placed second in the National Ranking Index-2020.

s: Who chaired the drafting committee of the National Education Policy 2020?
x: Dr K. Kasturirangan chaired the NEP 2020 drafting committee; the Cabinet approved it on 29 July 2020.

s: NEP 2020 targets a Gross Enrolment Ratio of 100% by 2030 at which level of education?
x: NEP 2020 targets 100% GER from pre-school to secondary by 2030. It is not limited to higher education, elementary classes 1-8 or vocational education.

s: What is the coverage of PM POSHAN?
x: PM POSHAN covers children from Bal Vatika through Class 8.

s: Which body developed the National Curriculum Frameworks for the Foundational Stage (2022) and School Education (2023)?
x: Both the NCF for Foundational Stage (2022) and the NCF for School Education (2023) were developed by NCERT.

s: Which age group does the Middle stage cover under the NEP 2020 school structure?
x: NEP 2020 stages: Foundational 3–8, Preparatory 8–11, Middle 11–14, Secondary 14–18 years.

s: With which of the following is PM POSHAN associated?
x: PM POSHAN concerns school meals; PM-SHRI is model schools, Vidya Pravesh school readiness and PARAKH assessment.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Samagra Shiksha integrates school education. ULLAS is adult literacy, DIKSHA the digital e-content platform and NIPUN Bharat foundational literacy and numeracy.

s: What is the school structure under NEP 2020?
x: NEP 2020 replaces 10+2 with a 5+3+3+4 structure.

s: Which of the following schemes linked to NEP 2020 is NOT correctly matched?
o: NIPUN Bharat – foundational literacy and numeracy
x: PARAKH deals with assessment; school meals are under PM POSHAN.

s: What level of public education spending does NEP 2020 target?
x: NEP 2020 targets public spending on education of 6% of GDP.

s: From which grade does NEP 2020 integrate vocational education with mainstream education?
x: NEP 2020 joins vocational education with mainstream education from Grade 6.

s: On which date did the Union Cabinet approve the National Education Policy 2020?
x: The Union Cabinet approved NEP 2020 on 29 July 2020; its drafting committee was chaired by K. Kasturirangan.

s: Which age group does the Foundational stage cover under the NEP 2020 school structure?
x: The Foundational stage of the 5+3+3+4 structure covers ages 3-8; Preparatory is 8-11.

s: What is human capital formation?
o: Transfer of all public resources from agriculture to services
Investment in education, health, skills, migration and information that raises people's productive capacity
Accumulation of foreign exchange reserves through international trade
Investment in physical infrastructure alone to increase industrial output
x: Human capital formation includes investment in education, health, skills acquired through on-the-job training, migration and information, all of which enhance people's productive capacity.

s: Which of the following is NOT a form of human capital formation?
x: Human capital formation covers education, health, skills (on-the-job training), migration and information; machinery is physical capital.

s:
Consider the following statements about human capital:
1. Human capital is the stock of skills, knowledge and health embodied in people.
2. Migration and information are not regarded as means of human capital formation; only education and health are.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: human capital is the stock of skills, knowledge and health in people. Statement 2 is wrong: human capital is formed through investment in education, health, on-the-job training, migration and information. So '1 only'.

s: What shift in education and health does the Economic Survey 2025-26 describe?
o: From public health to physical infrastructure exclusively
From access to quality and learning outcomes, along with preventive care
From quality to enrolment alone, without concern for outcomes
From preventive care to curative care alone
x: The stated policy shift is from access towards quality and learning outcomes, together with preventive care. Obesity and digital addiction are also emerging concerns.

s: What is India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR), cited among human capital indicators?
x: MMR is cited as 88 per lakh live births. 29.3% is the stunting rate and 19% the wasting rate, not MMR; 130 is not the cited figure, and MMR is expressed per lakh, not per thousand, live births.

s: What is the main reason for Kerala's low infant mortality rate?
o: Adequate basic health and education facilities
x: Kerala is the classic case where adequate basic health and education facilities produce a low infant mortality rate.

s: What is India's stunting rate, cited among human capital indicators?
x: The topic's human capital indicators cite stunting at 29.3% and wasting at 19%. (NFHS-5 put stunting at 35.5%; NFHS-3 at about 48%.)

s: Which of the following has no direct impact on human capital formation?
x: Human capital is formed through education, health, training, migration and information; irrigation has no direct impact.

s: Household out-of-pocket expenditure in 2022-23 was what share of total health expenditure?
x: OOPE was 43.4% of total health expenditure in 2022-23 (176th Report of the Standing Committee on Health).

s: What does the term 'missing middle' refer to in Indian health financing?
o: Urban households receiving both public and private health insurance
People fully covered by government subsidies but unable to access public hospitals
Only informal workers excluded from employment insurance
More than 40 crore people outside full subsidy coverage who cannot afford private care
x: The missing middle consists of more than 40 crore Indians who are outside full subsidy coverage but cannot afford private healthcare.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective associated with the National Health Policy 2017?
o: Restricting public health services exclusively to tertiary hospitals
Shifting emphasis from curative care to preventive and primary care
Raising public health spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2025
x: NHP 2017 envisaged higher public health spending, a shift toward preventive and primary care, and universal health coverage. It did not seek to restrict services to tertiary hospitals.

s: Who released the National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates for 2019-20 in April 2023?
o: Dr V.K. Paul, Member (Health), NITI Aayog
Dr K. Kasturirangan, Chairman of the NEP drafting committee
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
The National Health Authority's Chief Executive Officer
x: The NHA 2019-20 estimates were released in April 2023 by Dr V.K. Paul of NITI Aayog (PYQ). Dr Kasturirangan chaired the NEP 2020 drafting committee; the CAG audits accounts but did not release NHA; the National Health Authority runs PM-JAY and ABDM.

s: National Health Policy 2017 targets public health spending of what share of GDP by 2025?
x: NHP 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP by 2025; 6% is the NEP 2020 education target.

s: What is India's government health expenditure as a share of GDP, per the 176th Report of the Standing Committee on Health?
x: Government health spending is 1.43% of GDP against the 2.5% target; 4.89% is the health share of government spending.

s: Where was AB-PMJAY launched on 23 September 2018?
x: AB-PMJAY was launched at Ranchi (Jharkhand) on 23 September 2018.

s: What was the original beneficiary base of AB-PMJAY?
x: The scheme was based on approximately 12 crore families, covering around 55 crore people, corresponding broadly to the bottom 40 percent of the population.

s: Beneficiaries of AB-PMJAY were primarily identified using which basis?
x: The beneficiary base was identified using deprivation criteria from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011. States may widen the base at their own cost.

s: For how many days are pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses covered under AB-PMJAY?
x: PM-JAY covers 3 days of pre-hospitalisation and 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses.

s: What kind of care do Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (formerly Health and Wellness Centres) mainly provide?
x: Ayushman Arogya Mandir is the primary-care umbrella of Ayushman Bharat; primary care meets 80-90% of needs.

s: Which of the following groups was included in the 2024 expansion of PM-JAY?
o: Only pensioners receiving central government pensions
ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers and helpers, and their families
Only persons below 18 years of age
x: The 2024 expansion included ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers and helpers, along with their families.

s: What is the Centre-State funding pattern of AB-PMJAY?
o: 60:40, with 100% central funding in UTs without legislature
50:50, with States bearing the full cost in UTs
100% central funding in all States and UTs
x: AB-PMJAY is shared Centre-State 60:40, and the Centre bears 100% in UTs without legislature. 75:25 and 50:50 are not the PM-JAY ratios, and the scheme is not fully centrally funded in States.

s: Who is covered by the Ayushman Vay Vandana card under PM-JAY?
o: All persons aged 60+ below the poverty line
All persons aged 70+ regardless of income
x: Announced on 29 October 2024, it gives Rs 5 lakh cover to everyone aged 70+, with no income test.

s: Which States were the latest to join PM-JAY in April 2025?
x: Odisha and Delhi were the latest to join PM-JAY, in April 2025.

s: What is the health cover per family per year under AB-PMJAY?
x: AB-PMJAY gives a cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.

s:
Consider the following statements about AB-PMJAY:
1. It gives a health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
2. It is implemented by the National Health Authority.
3. Its beneficiaries were identified from Census 2011 income declarations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Cover is Rs 5 lakh and the NHA runs it; beneficiaries were identified by SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, not Census income data.

s: The Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) under ABDM is a health ID of how many digits?
x: ABHA is a 14-digit ID linking lifelong health records; participation is voluntary and consent-based.

s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the principal components of PM-ABHIM?
x: District critical-care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories, BSL-3 laboratories and surveillance are associated with PM-ABHIM. The four-registry architecture belongs to ABDM.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional character of PM-ABHIM and ABDM?
o: PM-ABHIM is a State Sector Scheme and ABDM is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
PM-ABHIM is a CSS with central components, while ABDM is a Central Sector initiative run by the National Health Authority.
Both are Central Sector Schemes run by the National Health Authority.
Both are implemented exclusively by State health departments.
x: PM-ABHIM has the character of a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with central components. ABDM is a Central Sector initiative run by the National Health Authority.

s: Where was PM-ABHIM launched in October 2021?
x: PM-ABHIM was launched at Varanasi in October 2021.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the four registries of ABDM?
x: ABDM's four registries are ABHA, HPR, HFR and the Drug Registry; Integrated Public Health Labs are part of PM-ABHIM.

s: What is the nature of creating an ABHA health ID under ABDM?
x: ABHA is voluntary and consent-based, not mandatory.

s: On which date was ABDM first announced as the National Digital Health Mission?
x: NDHM was announced on 15 August 2020; ABDM was launched in September 2021.

s: What is the outlay of PM-ABHIM over six years?
x: PM-ABHIM has an outlay of Rs 64,180 crore over six years for pandemic-ready health infrastructure.

s: Which agency gave a loan of US$ 1 billion for PM-ABHIM in July 2022?
x: The World Bank approved a US$ 1 billion loan in July 2022 to support PM-ABHIM.

s: Under PMSMA, free antenatal care is provided on which day of every month?
x: PMSMA (2016) gives free antenatal care to women in the second and third trimesters on the 9th of every month.

s: What is U-WIN?
o: Cash support scheme for institutional delivery
x: U-WIN is a digital vaccination registry; RKSK covers adolescent health, JSY institutional delivery and PMSMA antenatal care.

s: Which group is targeted by the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), launched in 2014?
x: RKSK targets adolescents aged 10-19.

s: For what purpose does Janani Suraksha Yojana (2005) give cash assistance to pregnant women?
o: Antenatal check-ups on the 9th of each month
x: JSY gives cash for institutional delivery; free antenatal care on the 9th is PMSMA.

s: In which year did NRHM become a sub-mission of the National Health Mission?
x: NRHM, launched in 2005, became a sub-mission of NHM in 2013 along with NUHM.

s: What is the aim of Mission Indradhanush, launched in December 2014?
o: Free antenatal care on the 9th of every month
Full immunisation of children under two and pregnant women
Digital health ID for every citizen
x: Mission Indradhanush aims at full immunisation of children under two and pregnant women against vaccine-preventable diseases.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) launched?
x: PMSMA was launched in 2016; it gives free antenatal care on the 9th of every month.

s: In which months are kharif crops generally sown in India?
x: Kharif crops are sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested around September–November.

s: On which of the following do rabi crops in India mainly depend?
x: Rabi crops are sown after monsoon withdrawal and depend substantially on western disturbances and irrigation.

s: The zaid season in India is generally characterised by which of the following?
o: A monsoon season beginning in June and ending in October
A rainfed season restricted to areas receiving less than 25 cm rainfall
A long winter season dependent on western disturbances
A short, irrigation-dependent summer window from March to June
x: Zaid is the short summer cropping window, generally extending from March to June, and it depends substantially on irrigation.

s: Which of the following season-crop pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cotton is a Kharif crop; wheat is Rabi and watermelon is Zaid.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a usual rabi crop?
x: Jute is a kharif crop. Wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas, linseed and potato are associated with the rabi season.

s: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?
x: Watermelon is a Zaid crop; jute is Kharif, while wheat and mustard are Rabi.

s:
Consider the following statements about pulses:
1. Tur (arhar) is a kharif crop.
2. Gram (chana) is a rabi crop.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tur/arhar is sown in kharif and gram/chana in rabi, so both statements are correct.

s: Which of the following crops is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons in Andhra Pradesh?
x: In AP, paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses are grown in both kharif and rabi.

s: In which season is jute grown in India?
x: Jute is a Kharif crop, not Rabi – a common trap.

s: What is the size of a semi-medium landholding?
x: Small holdings are 1–2 ha, semi-medium 2–4 ha, medium 4–10 ha and large 10 ha and above.

s: What was the average size of an operational holding in India as per the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
x: The average holding was 1.08 ha in 2015-16, down from 2.28 ha in 1971.

s: What is an operational holding?
o: Only irrigated land cultivated by a household
All land owned by a person, irrespective of whether it is cultivated
All land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit by one person, alone or with others, irrespective of title, size or location
Land recorded in the name of a single legal owner
x: An operational holding comprises land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit, regardless of title, size or location.

s: As per Agriculture Census 2010-11, small and marginal holdings were about 85% of holdings but operated about what share of the area?
x: In 2010-11 small and marginal holdings were about 85% of holdings but operated only about 44% of the area.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the largest average operational holding?
x: Ananthapuram has the largest average holding in AP at 1.62 ha; Visakhapatnam has the smallest at 0.40 ha.

s: What is the average operational holding in Andhra Pradesh as per the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22, provisional)?
x: AP's average holding fell from 0.94 ha to 0.86 ha; 1.08 ha is the all-India 2015-16 figure and 1.62 ha is Ananthapuram's average.

s: Women-operated holdings formed what share of operational holdings in the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
x: Women-operated holdings rose from 12.8% (2010-11) to 13.9% (2015-16).

s: Which State had the largest average operational holding in India as per the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
x: Nagaland had the largest average operational holding in 2015-16.

s: As per the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22, provisional), which AP district has the smallest average holding?
x: Visakhapatnam has the smallest average holding (0.40 ha); Ananthapuram has the largest (1.62 ha).

s: As per the Agriculture Census 2010-11, what was the average size of operational holdings held by Scheduled Castes?
x: In 2010-11 the average holding was 1.15 ha for all groups, 0.80 ha for SCs and 1.52 ha for STs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Agriculture Census 2010-11:
1. The average holding of Scheduled Tribes was larger than the all-groups average.
2. The average holding of Scheduled Castes was smaller than the all-groups average.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: STs held 1.52 ha and SCs 0.80 ha on average, against 1.15 ha for all groups.

s: How many operational holdings did Andhra Pradesh have as per the 11th Agriculture Census 2021-22 (provisional)?
x: AP's holdings rose from 85.24 lakh to 96.90 lakh, with the average falling to 0.86 ha.

s: As per the Agriculture Census 2015-16, what share of all operational holdings were small and marginal holdings?
x: Small and marginal holdings were 86.2% of holdings but operated only 47.3% of the area in 2015-16.

s: How many operational holdings did India have as per the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
x: The 10th Agriculture Census (2015-16) counted 146 million operational holdings.

s:
Consider the following statements about operational holdings in India:
1. The average holding was 2.28 ha in 1971.
2. The average holding rose to 1.08 ha in 2015-16 from 1.15 ha in 2010-11.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The average holding fell from 2.28 ha (1971) to 1.15 ha (2010-11) and 1.08 ha (2015-16), showing fragmentation; it did not rise.

s: What was India's cropping intensity in 2021-22?
x: Cropping intensity = GCA ÷ NSA × 100 = 219.16 ÷ 141 × 100, about 155.4% in 2021-22.

s: Which of the following is a category of the nine-fold land-use classification of India?
x: Current fallows is one of the nine land-use categories. Net irrigated area and the gross measures are not among them.

s: Which land-use measure counts a plot once for each crop grown on it?
x: Gross cropped area counts repeated cropping, so it is generally larger than net sown area, which counts a plot only once.

s: What was India's net sown area in 2021-22?
x: Net sown area was 141 Mha (42.8% of geographical area); 219.16 Mha is the gross cropped area.

s: How is cropping intensity calculated?
x: Cropping intensity = gross cropped area ÷ net sown area × 100, about 155.4% for India in 2021-22.

s: What share of India's geographical area was net sown area in 2021-22?
x: India's net sown area of 141 Mha was 42.8% of its 328.7 Mha geographical area.

s: As per ISFR 2021, what share of India's geographical area is under forest cover?
x: ISFR 2021 puts forest cover at 21.71% of India's geographical area.

s: What is the geographical area of India used in land-use statistics?
x: India's geographical area is 328.7 Mha; net sown area is 141 Mha and gross cropped area 219.16 Mha (2021-22).

s: What share of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area is under forests in its land-use classification?
x: Forests are 22.63%; net area sown is 36.29%, current fallows 8.96% and barren land 8.19%.

s: Which is the largest land-use category in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Net area sown (36.29%) is AP's largest category, followed by forests (22.63%).

s: Which is the smallest land-use category in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Miscellaneous tree crops cover only 0.94% of AP, the smallest category; culturable waste is 2.47%.

s: What was the cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24?
x: AP's cropping intensity was 1.21 in 2023-24, below India's about 1.55 (155.4%).

s: What is the geographical area of Andhra Pradesh as per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26?
x: AP's geographical area is 162.97 lakh ha; net area sown is 59.14 lakh ha of it.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, agriculture employs about what share of India's workforce?
x: Agriculture employs 46.1% of the workforce and contributes nearly one-fifth of national income at current prices.

s: What was the average growth rate of Indian agriculture during FY16-FY25?
x: Agriculture recorded an average growth of 4.4% during FY16-FY25, described as its highest decadal growth rate.

s: What record level did India's agricultural exports reach?
x: Agri exports hit a record $51.91 billion, about 11.86% of merchandise exports.

s: Horticulture accounts for about what share of India's agricultural GVA?
x: Horticulture is about 33% (one-third) of agricultural GVA, not half; in 2024-25 its output (367.72 MT) overtook foodgrains (357.73 MT).

s: What is agriculture's approximate share in India's GVA as per the Economic Survey 2025-26?
x: Agriculture contributes about 18% of GVA, nearly one-fifth of national income, though it employs 46.1% of workers.

s: Which of the following is NOT a role of agriculture in the Indian economy?
o: Contributing the largest share of GVA
Supplying raw material such as cotton and jute to industry
x: Agriculture supplies raw material, food security and exports, but its GVA share (~18%) is far below its employment share, not the largest.

s: In 2024-25, horticulture output in India was about 367.72 MT. How did it compare with foodgrains?
o: It was less than half of foodgrains
It passed foodgrains output of 357.73 MT
It was a quarter of foodgrains output
x: Horticulture output (367.72 MT) overtook foodgrains (357.73 MT) in 2024-25.

s: The post-1991 liberalisation period was followed by a decline in which of the following in Indian agriculture?
x: Liberalisation after 1991 was followed by a decline in government (public) investment in agriculture.

s: In which year did the WTO Agreement on Agriculture come into effect?
x: The WTO Agreement on Agriculture took effect in 1995.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a principal area of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
x: The Agreement on Agriculture covers market access, domestic support and export subsidies; land ceilings are a domestic land-reform matter.

s: Which of the following was a component of the Agricultural Renewal Action Plan (APPSC Group-II 2017)?
x: The plan covered soil health, irrigation/water augmentation with demand management, and credit and insurance; boosting capital formation was not a component.

s: Which crop has the largest cropped area in India (about 51-52 million ha)?
x: Rice has the largest cropped area in India, about 51-52 million hectares.

s: Why is shifting about 20% of rice area to pulses and legumes proposed?
o: Reduce urea use and conserve groundwater
x: The proposed shift aims to reduce urea use and save groundwater.

s: Which one of the following best describes the long-term trend in India's cropping pattern?
o: A uniform increase in the area under all food and non-food crops
A shift from commercial crops towards subsistence food crops only
A shift from food crops towards commercial and high-value crops
A complete replacement of rice and wheat by millets
x: India has experienced a long-run shift from food crops to commercial and high-value crops, influenced by irrigation, prices and technology.

s: What mainly drove rice-wheat expansion during 2015-2025 in States like Punjab, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh?
x: Assured MSP procurement drove rice-wheat expansion in these States.

s: Which State has the largest area under soyabean in India?
x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest soyabean area, followed by Maharashtra.

s: Which crop occupies the largest area among the foodgrain crops of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Paddy is AP's largest foodgrain crop: 20.97 of 37.51 lakh ha of foodgrain area in 2024-25 (2nd AE). Pulses as a group come next at 11.66 lakh ha, and maize at 3.20 lakh ha.

s: How has groundnut area changed in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Groundnut area in AP declined from 11.36 to 3.46 lakh ha, while jowar and ragi also shrank.

s: Towards which crops was a shift planned in response to the rainfall conditions of Kharif 2026?
x: The planned response included shifting towards pulses and drought-resilient crops in view of the deficient rainfall conditions.

s: The expansion of maize cultivation in the Godavari–Krishna belt is mainly associated with demand from which sectors?
x: Maize cultivation is expanding in the Godavari–Krishna belt because of demand for poultry feed and starch.

s: Which one of the following is a major agricultural constraint identified for Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's listed constraints are monsoon dependence, fragmented holdings below one hectare, soil-fertility loss and weak credit.

s: After paddy, which is the largest foodgrain group by area in Andhra Pradesh (2024-25)?
x: Pulses (11.66 lakh ha) follow paddy (20.97 lakh ha); maize has 3.20 lakh ha.

s: Oil palm cultivation is expanding in which AP districts?
x: Oil palm is expanding in East Godavari, Eluru and West Godavari.

s: Which crop is called the 'white gold' of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Cotton, an expanding commercial crop, is called the 'white gold' of Andhra Pradesh.

s: What was the area under foodgrains in Andhra Pradesh in 2021-22?
x: AP's foodgrain area was 41.44 lakh ha in 2021-22, then 33.24 (2023-24) and 37.51 lakh ha (2024-25).

s: What does a faster growth of area under non-food crops than under food crops in a State indicate?
x: A shift of area from food crops to non-food (cash) crops shows farming is becoming more market-oriented, i.e. commercialised.

s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of food crops?
x: Food crops comprise cereals, millets and pulses. Cotton, jute, sugarcane, tobacco and several oilseeds are classified as commercial or cash crops.

s: Which of the following is a traditional commercial crop of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Groundnut, cotton, tobacco and sugarcane are AP's traditional commercial crops; paddy, jowar and ragi are traditional food crops.

s: Which of the following make up foodgrains in India?
x: Foodgrains = cereals + pulses; oilseeds are a separate group.

s: Which was the first commercial GM crop in India, approved in 2002?
x: Bt cotton (2002) is India's only major GM crop; Bt brinjal is under moratorium since 2010.

s:
Consider the following statements about GM crops in India:
1. Bt brinjal has been under a moratorium since 2010.
2. GM mustard DMH-11 received GEAC environmental-release approval in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Bt brinjal is under moratorium since 2010, and DMH-11 got the GEAC nod in 2022 (pending in the Supreme Court).

s: Which was the largest source of India's net irrigated area in 2021-22?
x: Tubewells provided 47.3% of net irrigated area, followed by canals (24.7%), other wells (13.2%), other sources (12%) and tanks (2.8%).

s: What was India's net irrigated area in 2021-22?
x: Net irrigated area was 77.9 Mha; 120.3 Mha is the gross irrigated area.

s: After tubewells, which was the second-largest contributor to India's net irrigated area in 2021-22?
x: Canals contributed 24.7%, second to tubewells (47.3%); tanks were only 2.8%.

s: Canal irrigation in the northern plains of India is fed mainly by which kind of rivers?
x: Himalayan rivers are perennial (snow-fed), so they can feed canals all year; peninsular areas rely more on tanks.

s: About what share of India's net sown area is rainfed?
x: About 51-52% of India's net sown area is rainfed; irrigation covers about 67% of rice area.

s: What was India's gross irrigated area in 2021-22?
x: In 2021-22 the net irrigated area was 77.9 Mha and the gross irrigated area 120.3 Mha.

s: Irrigation covers about 67% of rice area in India. What share of pulses area is irrigated?
x: Only about 26% of pulses area is irrigated, against 67% of rice area; pulses are largely rainfed.

s: How many soil categories are found in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has 22 soil categories, of which 10 cover over 88% of the State.

s: On what basis are the agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh defined?
o: Climate, soil, topography and factors determining the suitable cropping system
x: The zones are defined by climate, soil, topography and other factors that determine the best cropping system.

s: Which of the following is one of the Planning Commission's agro-climatic regions?
x: Trans-Gangetic Plains is a Planning Commission region; Central Coastal Delta is not, and Godavari and Scarce Rainfall are AP's own zones.

s: Andhra Pradesh falls within which of the following Planning Commission agro-climatic regions?
o: East Coast Plains and Hills and Southern Plateau and Hills
Central Plateau and Hills and Western Dry Region
Eastern Himalayan and Lower Gangetic Plains
x: The coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh fall in the East Coast Plains and Hills region, while Rayalaseema falls in the Southern Plateau and Hills region.

s: The NARP classification divided India into how many agro-climatic zones?
x: NARP divided India into 127 agro-climatic zones; the Planning Commission identified 15 regions with 72 sub-zones.

s: How many agro-climatic zones does the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 list?
x: APSES 2024-25 lists six zones (still on the 13 pre-2022 districts); older material and the 2017 Group-II key used seven.

s: Which of the following pre-2022 agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched with its districts?
o: North Coastal – Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
x: The North Coastal Zone comprised Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Godavari had East/West Godavari, Krishna had Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam, and Southern had Chittoor, YSR Kadapa, SPS Nellore.

s: The Scarce Rainfall Zone of Andhra Pradesh comprises which districts and has which zonal headquarters?
x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone comprises Kurnool and Anantapuramu, with its zonal headquarters at Nandyal.

s: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had how many agro-climatic zones?
x: Undivided AP had nine zones; the 2017 key had seven and APSES 2024-25 lists six.

s: Where is the zonal headquarters (RARS) of the Godavari Zone, known as the 'Rice Bowl'?
x: Maruteru is the RARS of the Godavari Zone; Nandyal serves Scarce Rainfall and Chintapalle the High Altitude and Tribal Zone.

s: Into how many regions and sub-zones did the Planning Commission's agro-climatic regionalisation (1989) divide India?
x: The Planning Commission set 15 regions with 72 sub-zones; NARP has 127 zones.

s: Where is the zonal headquarters (RARS) of the High Altitude and Tribal Zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The High Altitude and Tribal Zone (agency areas) has its RARS at Chintapalle; Maruteru serves the Godavari Zone and Nandyal the Scarce Rainfall Zone.

s: Which districts formed the Southern Zone among the pre-2022 agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore
x: The Southern Zone had Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore; Kurnool and Anantapuramu formed the Scarce Rainfall Zone.

s: Which State has the largest tubewell-irrigated area in India?
x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest tubewell-irrigated area in India.

s: Why are tanks particularly important sources of irrigation in peninsular States?
x: Tanks are important in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu because these regions have undulating hard-rock terrain.

s: Groundwater meets about what share of India's irrigation needs?
x: Groundwater meets about 64% of India's irrigation needs; India accounts for about 25% of global groundwater extraction.

s: Tanks provide what share of India's net irrigated area (2021-22)?
x: Tanks provide only 2.8%, though they matter in peninsular hard-rock States.

s: India accounts for about what share of global groundwater extraction?
x: India extracts about 25% of the world's groundwater, and groundwater meets about 64% of its irrigation needs.

s: On which date was the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) launched?
x: PMKSY, the umbrella irrigation scheme, was launched on 1 July 2015.

s: Which PMKSY component deals with micro-irrigation?
x: Per Drop More Crop covers micro-irrigation (now under PM-RKVY); Har Khet Ko Pani covers assured irrigation and CAD.

s: What is the corpus of the Micro Irrigation Fund with NABARD?
x: The Micro Irrigation Fund has a corpus of Rs 5,000 crore with NABARD.

s: From which date did the Hariyali guidelines for watershed development come into force?
x: Hariyali guidelines took effect from 1 April 2003.

s: Hariyali, IWDP and NWDPRA were merged into which programme in 2008?
x: They were merged into the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) under the 2008 common guidelines.

s: Which agency supports the Neeranchal National Watershed Project?
x: Neeranchal is World Bank-aided ($178.5 million), covering nine States including AP and Telangana.

s: How did the Centre-State funding pattern for watershed projects change under WDC-PMKSY?
x: Funding under WDC-PMKSY moved from 90:10 to 60:40.

s: Who founded the Rajasthan NGO Tarun Bharat Sangh?
x: Tarun Bharat Sangh, a water-conservation NGO of Rajasthan, was founded by Dr Rajendra Singh.

s: Who chairs the State Level Sanctioning Committee under PMKSY?
x: Under PMKSY, District Irrigation Plans feed State plans, sanctioned by a committee chaired by the Chief Secretary.

s: The World Bank-aided Neeranchal National Watershed Project covers how many States?
x: Neeranchal (World Bank, $178.5 million) covers nine States, including Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: What does WDC 2.0 add to watershed development under PMKSY?
x: WDC 2.0, the watershed component of PMKSY, adds springshed development.

s: With which institution was the Watershed Development Fund set up in 1999-2000?
x: The Watershed Development Fund was set up at NABARD in 1999-2000 with a corpus of Rs 200 crore shared by the Centre and NABARD.

s: What is the Right Canal of Nagarjuna Sagar called?
x: The Nagarjuna Sagar Right Canal is the Jawahar Canal; the Left Canal is the Lal Bahadur Shastri Canal.

s: From where does the Indira Gandhi Canal draw its water?
o: Krishna through the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir
Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas system
x: The Indira Gandhi Canal originates at Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas system and runs in Rajasthan.

s: Which canal is correctly matched with its source?
o: Indira Gandhi Canal – Sutlej at Ropar
Upper Ganga Canal – Ganga at Haridwar
x: The Upper Ganga Canal (UP) draws from the Ganga at Haridwar; the Sirhind Canal (Punjab) draws from the Sutlej at Ropar and the Indira Gandhi Canal from Harike barrage.

s: From where does the Sirhind Canal draw water?
x: Sirhind Canal in Punjab takes off from the Sutlej at Ropar.

s: What is the Left Canal of Nagarjuna Sagar called?
x: Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna has the Jawahar (Right) Canal and the Lal Bahadur Shastri (Left) Canal.

s: Which State is mainly irrigated by the Indira Gandhi Canal, about 650 km long?
x: The Indira Gandhi Canal takes Sutlej-Beas water from Harike barrage to Rajasthan.

s: What kind of scheme is the World Bank-aided Atal Bhujal Yojana, launched in December 2019?
o: State Sector scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development
Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti
Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Agriculture
x: Atal Bhujal Yojana was launched in December 2019 as a World Bank-aided Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

s: Which of the following States was NOT among the seven States covered by Atal Bhujal Yojana?
x: The seven States covered were Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh was not included in that list.

s: What is the principal focus of Atal Bhujal Yojana?
o: Demand-side community management through Gram Panchayat Water Security Plans
x: Atal Bhujal focuses on demand-side groundwater management through community participation and Gram Panchayat-level Water Security Plans.

s: Which of the following is a stage-of-extraction category used in the Central Ground Water Board assessment?
x: The CGWB categories are Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited and Saline; 'adequately exploited' is not one of them.

s: What is India's stage of groundwater extraction as of 2025?
x: India's stage of extraction was 60.63% in 2025, up from 60.47% in 2024.

s: In which part of India have GRACE satellite studies shown severe groundwater depletion?
x: GRACE studies show severe depletion in north-west India - Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi.

s: Since when has the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) been in operation?
x: APMIP has been operating since 2003.

s: Under which component of PM-KUSUM does solarisation of grid-connected pumps, including feeder-level solarisation, fall?
x: Component C covers grid-connected pump solarisation; Component A is 10,000 MW of decentralised plants and Component B the 14 lakh standalone pumps.

s: Under which ministry was PM-KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan) launched in 2019?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).

s: Which one of the following best captures the principal concern regarding widespread installation of solar pumps?
o: They prevent the use of drip irrigation.
They necessarily reduce all agricultural incomes.
They may encourage over-drawing of groundwater.
They can operate only in major irrigation command areas.
x: Solar pumps may reduce diesel dependence but can also encourage groundwater over-draw. The outcome depends on local hydrogeology.

s: What does Component B of PM-KUSUM provide for?
x: Component B covers 14 lakh standalone solar pumps (up to 7.5 HP); A is 10,000 MW plants and C is pump solarisation.

s: Which State ranks first in micro-irrigation in India?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in micro-irrigation, through APMIP running since 2003.

s: Which region accounts for about 64% of the area under the AP Micro Irrigation Project?
x: Rayalaseema accounts for 64% of APMIP's 42.25 lakh acres.

s:
Consider the following statements about drip irrigation:
