1. It delivers water directly to the root zone of plants.
2. It allows fertilisers to be applied along with irrigation water (fertigation).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Drip sends water straight to the root zone, and soluble fertiliser can be given through the same lines (fertigation).

s: What does Component A of PM-KUSUM provide for?
o: 10,000 MW of decentralised grid-connected solar plants
x: Component A is 10,000 MW of small (0.5-2 MW) grid-connected solar plants; B is standalone pumps and C is solarisation of grid pumps.

s: What is the full form of APWALTA?
o: Andhra Pradesh Watershed and Land Taxation Act, 2005
Andhra Pradesh Water and Irrigation Regulation Act, 2015
Andhra Pradesh Water Allocation and Land Tenure Act, 2002
Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002
x: APWALTA is the Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002, which addresses issues including indiscriminate borewell digging.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Water, Land and Trees Act (APWALTA), 2002:
1. Rainwater harvesting structures are mandatory on plots of 200 sq m and above.
2. Rainwater harvesting structures are mandatory only on plots of 1,000 sq m and above.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: APWALTA requires rainwater harvesting on plots of 200 sq m and above, so statement 2's 1,000 sq m threshold is wrong.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Polavaram Project:
1. It has an installed power capacity of 960 MW.
2. It diverts 80 TMC of water to the Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Polavaram has a 960 MW capacity and diverts 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna; both statements are correct.

s: The Polavaram project was recently reported to be about what per cent complete?
x: Polavaram was reported 89% complete and targeted for dedication by March 2027.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's stage of groundwater development as per the Ground Water Estimation (GEC 2024-25)?
x: AP's stage of development is 31.5%, which is Safe; only 12 of its 679 mandals are over-exploited. 60.63% is India's all-India stage of extraction (2025), and 64% is groundwater's share of India's irrigation needs; AP as a whole is not over-exploited.

s: Which of the following AP projects is NOT based on the Krishna?
x: Polavaram is a Godavari project; Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda and Nagarjuna Sagar are Krishna-based.

s:
Consider the following statements about AP irrigation projects:
1. Polavaram is a National Project under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
2. Veligonda draws Krishna water through Srisailam tunnels.
3. Galeru-Nagari is a Godavari-based project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Polavaram is a National Project (APRA 2014) and Veligonda takes Krishna water via Srisailam tunnels; Galeru-Nagari is Krishna-based, not Godavari.

s: How many irrigation tanks does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP has 38,862 tanks with an ayacut of 25.60 lakh acres.

s: After whom is the Veligonda project of Andhra Pradesh named?
x: Veligonda is the Poola Subbaiah project; it draws Krishna water through Srisailam tunnels.

s: About what share of the gross irrigated area of Andhra Pradesh is served by groundwater (2024-25)?
x: Groundwater irrigates about 41% of AP's gross irrigated area of 36.77 lakh ha, through about 19 lakh borewells.

s: How many mandals of Andhra Pradesh were over-exploited as per the Ground Water Estimation (GEC 2024-25)?
x: 12 of 679 mandals were over-exploited, 3 critical, 24 semi-critical and 39 saline; 601 were safe.

s: By when is the Polavaram project targeted to be dedicated to the nation?
x: Polavaram was about 89% complete and is targeted for dedication by March 2027.

s: What was the gross irrigated area of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: AP's gross irrigated area was 36.77 lakh ha and net irrigated area 30.33 lakh ha in 2024-25.

s: From which reservoir does the Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi lift canal draw Krishna water for Rayalaseema?
x: HNSS lifts Krishna flood water from the Srisailam backwaters at Malyala (Kurnool) to Kurnool, Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor.

s: What was the main aim of the Neeru-Chettu programme launched by Andhra Pradesh in 2015?
o: Supplying piped drinking water to cities
Making the State drought-free through water conservation
Linking the Godavari and Krishna rivers
Giving free power to farm pump sets
x: Neeru-Chettu (2015) aimed to make AP drought-free through water conservation, chiefly by desilting minor irrigation tanks and building check dams and farm ponds.

s: Minor irrigation provides about what share of India's irrigated area?
x: Minor irrigation (CCA up to 2,000 ha) provides about 65% of India's irrigated area.

s: What is the main aim of the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP)?
o: Speed up ongoing major and medium irrigation projects
x: AIBP is meant to accelerate completion of ongoing major and medium irrigation projects.

s: What is the Culturable Command Area of a minor irrigation project?
x: Minor projects cover up to 2,000 ha CCA; medium 2,000-10,000 ha; major above 10,000 ha.

s: What is the Culturable Command Area of a major irrigation project?
x: Major projects have CCA above 10,000 ha; 2,000-10,000 ha is medium.

s: Since 2016, how many prioritised AIBP projects are funded through NABARD's Long Term Irrigation Fund?
x: 99 prioritised AIBP projects (8 in AP) are funded through NABARD's LTIF.

s: How many of the 99 prioritised AIBP projects funded through NABARD's LTIF are in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Eight of the 99 prioritised AIBP projects are in Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about irrigation efficiency:
1. Drip irrigation is about 90% efficient.
2. Flood or basin surface irrigation is about 30–50% efficient.
3. Flood irrigation is more water-efficient than drip irrigation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Drip (about 90%) is far more efficient than flood/basin irrigation (30–50%), so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Direct Seeded Rice can save up to how much water?
x: Direct Seeded Rice (like SRI) can save up to 50% water.

s: Why is micro-irrigation particularly effective in conserving water?
o: sends water directly to the root zone and reduces evaporation and runoff
raises water application above the crop canopy
increases surface runoff from cultivated fields
x: Micro-irrigation delivers water directly to the roots and reduces losses through evaporation and runoff.

s: How does zero or minimum tillage mainly save irrigation water?
o: Lowering evaporation and keeping soil moisture
x: Less soil disturbance lowers evaporation and keeps soil moisture; more weeds is its drawback.

s: What is the minimum permanent soil cover under FAO's Conservation Agriculture?
x: Conservation Agriculture asks for permanent soil cover of at least 30%, with minimum disturbance and crop diversification.

s: Which irrigation method has an efficiency of about 70-80%?
x: Sprinkler is about 70-80% efficient; drip is ~90% and flood/basin 30-50%.

s: Who gave the concept of 'virtual water'?
x: Tony Allan coined 'virtual water' - the water used to produce a product; exporting rice exports virtual water.

s: How is per capita annual water availability below 1,700 cubic metres classified?
x: Per capita annual water availability below 1,700 m³ is treated as water-stressed.

s: Per capita annual water availability below which level is classified as water-scarce?
x: Availability below 1,000 m³ per person per year is classified as water-scarce.

s: Which was the first State in India to approve a draft State Water Policy?
x: Meghalaya was the first State to approve a draft State Water Policy (APPSC 2019 key). Tamil Nadu was first to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory; Andhra Pradesh's measure is APWALTA 2002; Gujarat tops the Composite Water Management Index.

s: Inter-State rivers and river valleys are covered by which entry of the Union List?
x: Inter-State rivers are Entry 56 of the Union List, while water is Entry 17 of the State List.

s: India's per capita annual water availability places it in which category?
x: India is already below 1,700 m³ per capita, so it is water-stressed.

s: Water, as a subject, falls under which entry of the Constitution?
x: Water is Entry 17 of the State List; inter-State rivers are Entry 56 of the Union List.

s: Which was the first State to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings?
x: Tamil Nadu was the first to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory; Meghalaya was first with a draft State Water Policy.

s: The Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed in May 2019 by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation
x: In May 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

s: Who chairs the National Water Resources Council?
x: The National Water Resources Council is chaired by the Prime Minister; Chief Ministers are its members.

s: Which of the following is NOT a focus area of the National Water Policy, 2012?
o: Complete replacement of State water institutions by a single Union authority
x: The policy focuses on recycling and reuse, micro-irrigation incentives and community participation, among other measures. It does not prescribe complete replacement of State water institutions by one Union authority.

s: By how much does the National Water Mission aim to raise water-use efficiency?

s: In which year was India's first National Water Policy adopted?

s: Under which body does the Bureau of Water Use Efficiency (BWUE), set up in October 2022, function?

s: How many water-stressed districts did the Jal Shakti Abhiyan (2019) focus on?

s: Which body did the Mihir Shah Committee (2016) recommend by merging the CWC and the CGWB?

s: Which of the following is a criticism of the National River Linking Project?

Surplus river basins may become unreliable because of climate change
